questions.text:
1. In today's contemporary online shopping landscape, a perfect storm of choice engulfs consumers. Research consistently indicates that individuals presented with a limited selection tend to make more confident and efficient decisions compared to those confronted with overwhelming choices.
2. Consequently, assisting consumers in navigating the vast expanse of options available online has evolved into a thriving industry on a global scale. Many brands and retailers now employ marketing strategies revolving around the aspects given in the table below:

| Aspect | Description |
|---|---|
| Industry | Helping consumers decide what to buy online. |
| Marketing tools | Selecting, differentiation and discovery. |
| Data utilization | Digital advertising, cataloging people by gender, income level, personal interests and more. |
| Retail Assistance | Algorithms, influencers and ad tech. |
| Challenge | Choice fatigue due to the overwhelming volume of consumer choices. |
| Solution | Lifestyle influencers on Instagram providing aspirational content and product recommendations. |

3. For a relatively new breed of consumer product startups, a different approach emerges entirely. Rather than attempting to navigate the existing sea of products, these companies claim to revolutionize conventional consumer choices. Some brands offer limited, functional, mid-priced products, instilling customer confidence and breaking the cycle of consumerism.
4. The global product abundance could be more equitable. Unfortunately, creators often prioritize wealthier consumers.
5. For startups promising accessible simplicity, their very structure may eventually lead them back to an overwhelming array of choices. Most of these companies rely on hundreds of millions of dollars in venture capital funding, and their inventors typically expect rapid growth.
(Adapted for academic usage)

1. Monsoon is the most delightful season: dark clouds adding drama to the skies, air fragrant with the unmatched scent of wet earth getting drenched in the rains.
2. This one is for nostalgia. Though recently a neighbouring small town called Mawsynram has overtaken it, Cherrapunji is forever etched in our memories as the wettest place on earth. It may be officially the second wettest place, but that's still a lot of rain to revel in ! The best part about Sohra, as it is locally called, is that unlike other hill stations in the northeast, the roads are in good condition and driving in the rain is not a hazard. There are several waterfalls and viewpoints, including the milky white Nohkalikai Falls, which at 340 metres, is among the tallest waterfalls in the country.

Read the following passage carefully:
1. For centuries, millets were a staple on Indian plates. Hardy and drought-resistant, they grew well in dry regions where wheat and rice struggled. After the Green Revolution, however, cheap and plentiful rice and wheat pushed them to the margins, and millets came to be dismissed as the 'food of the poor'.
2. In recent years, nutritionists have changed that verdict. Millets are rich in fibre and minerals, and they release sugar slowly into the blood, which makes them a sensible choice for people worried about diabetes. Farmers, too, like them: they need little water and few chemical fertilisers, and they can survive uncertain rains.
3. Three of the best-known millets are shown in the table below.

| Millet | English name | Chief growing region | Notable benefit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ragi | Finger millet | Karnataka | Rich in calcium |
| Bajra | Pearl millet | Rajasthan | Rich in iron |
| Jowar | Sorghum | Maharashtra | High in fibre |

4. The challenge now is to make millets attractive to young city consumers who find them unfamiliar. Chefs and food start-ups are turning them into pasta, biscuits and dosas, and a few schools have added millet laddoos to the midday meal. If such efforts continue, an old grain may well become the new favourite.

questions.text:
The Pros and Cons of using the internet in everyday life are numerous. The internet is like a double-edged sword. Based on the information provided in the table below, write an analytical paragraph on the topic 'Advantages and Disadvantages of the Internet'.

Pros and Cons of Internet

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| (1) Connectivity | (1) Data Security |
| (2) Communication speed and versatile working | (2) Social Isolation |
| (3) Learning Re-defined | (3) Addiction towards it |
| (4) Transfer of Data | (4) Plagiarism and copyright |
questions.answer:
Analytical Paragraph: Advantages and Disadvantages of the Internet
The internet has become an integral part of everyday life, offering numerous benefits along with certain drawbacks. One of its key advantages is connectivity, enabling people across the world to stay linked instantly. It also enhances communication speed and supports versatile working, making tasks quicker and more efficient. The internet has redefined learning by providing easy access to information, online courses, and educational resources. Additionally, it allows fast transfer of data, supporting both personal and professional needs.
However, the internet also poses challenges. Data security is a major concern as online platforms are vulnerable to hacking and misuse. Excessive use of the internet can lead to social isolation, reducing real-life interactions. Many users, especially youth, may develop addiction, affecting their productivity. Moreover, plagiarism and copyright violations have increased due to the easy availability of online content.
Thus, while the internet is highly useful, its responsible use is essential.

or.text:
In the past few years, the teaching-learning process has taken a leap and gone beyond the four walls of the classroom. Today, it has become possible to learn not just by sitting in a physical classroom, but from anywhere. Given below is a chart depicting the differences between E-learning and Classroom learning. Write an analytical paragraph, assessing the benefits and drawbacks of both, by selecting features that support your analysis.

| E-learning | vs. | Classroom learning |
|---|---|---|
| accessible anytime anywhere; at your own pace; no travel costs, saves time | | same place, same time; caters to the needs of the class; transportation cost and time consuming |
or.answer: The shift from traditional classrooms to digital platforms has transformed the teaching-learning process. E-learning offers flexible access to lessons anytime and anywhere, allowing students to learn at their own pace. It eliminates travel, saving both time and money. Classroom learning, in contrast, requires students to be present at the same place and time, which may not suit individual learning needs. However, it provides direct interaction with teachers and peers, catering effectively to the needs of the entire class. It also involves transportation costs and additional time. Therefore, both methods have clear benefits and drawbacks: e-learning is convenient and economical, while classroom learning supports structured guidance and personal engagement.

"As soon as he has leapt on you,
You'll know it is the Leopard."

subparts.text: i. Which animal is being identified in these lines? (1)
subparts.answer: The Leopard.

subparts.text: ii. What does the poet suggest about the usefulness of such a description for a traveller? (2)
subparts.answer: The poet suggests it is of no practical use, because the animal is identified only after it has already attacked; the exaggeration makes the poem funny rather than instructive.

subparts.text: iii. What does the phrase 'leapt on you' suggest about the animal? (1)
subparts.answer: That it is a fast, powerful animal that attacks suddenly.

The poem teaches readers a serious method of identifying wild animals.
subparts.answer: False. The poem is a humorous nonsense verse and not a real guide.

questions.text: Answer ANY FOUR of the following five questions, in about 50 words each.

subparts.text: What did the bakers wear when the author was young?
subparts.answer: The bakers in the Portuguese days were very simple. They wore a peculiar dress that was a long single piece of frock reaching down to the knees. It was called the 'kabai'. The author described that when he was young, the bakers wore a shirt and a trouser that was longer than half pants and shorter than full pants. This symbolised the identity of a baker.

subparts.text: It is our attitude towards a situation that makes it positive or negative. Do you agree with it? Express your views with reference to the poem, Dust of Snow.
subparts.answer: Whatever situation life throws at us, it evokes both positive and negative responses. The poet, in the poem, "Dust of Snow" was in a sorrowful mood. However, when a crow shook down the 'dust of snow' on him, his bitter mood changed into a more optimistic one. Now, being in a sorrowful or bad mood already, the poet could have got angry at the crow also. However, the dust of snow becomes a positive medium of change for him. It made him cheerful to some extent and helped him forget his sadness, at least for a few moments. Thus, we see that instead of seeing the negative aspect of a happening, one should see the positive aspect, and one's response may greatly affect the outcome of incidents.

subparts.text: What idea does the Postmaster come up with? What did he do to stick to his resolution? (A Letter to God)
subparts.answer: The Postmaster comes up with the idea to answer Lencho's letter to God in order to maintain Lencho's faith. To stick to his resolution, the Postmaster gathers money from his employees, contributes part of his own salary, and persuades several friends to donate as well, pooling together what they can. Despite not being able to gather the full amount Lencho requested, the Postmaster sends Lencho a little more than half of it in an envelope, accompanied by a letter signed with the single word "God". This act reflects the Postmaster's attempt to uphold Lencho's belief in divine assistance, even though the response falls short of Lencho's expectations.

subparts.text: Why does Anne want to keep a diary?
subparts.answer: Anne didn't have any real friends to share her feelings and thoughts with. Further, she believed that paper had more patience than people and so she wanted to get all kinds of things off her chest and confide her innermost perceptions of different things with the diary.

subparts.text: What role does each of Belinda's pets play in the narrative? Select any two of her pets. (The Tale of Custard the Dragon)
subparts.answer: Belinda's pets add humour and ridicule to the narrative by constantly mocking Custard, the dragon, for his supposed cowardice. Mustard, the dog, boasted loudly about his courage and often bullied Custard to appear brave. Ink, the black cat, portrayed with a sense of mystery like witchcraft, also joined in teasing and belittling him. Even Blink, the tiny mouse - shown as timid and known to be the first to abandon danger - mocked Custard despite his own weaknesses. Ironically, Custard, who was meek, timid, and fearful despite being a dragon, was the only one who bravely fought the pirate and saved the household. This contrast creates humour and highlights the true meaning of courage.

questions.text: Answer ANY TWO of the following three questions, in about 40-50 words.
questions.answer:
1. The young seagull was afraid that his wings would not support him and that he would fall into the sea. His brothers and sister had already flown, but he stayed on the ledge. His mother tempted the hungry bird with a piece of fish, and he finally leapt, found his wings and flew.
2. On a dark stormy night the pilot saw a black aeroplane with no lights flying beside him. Tired and anxious, he followed it through the clouds and reached the airfield safely. The controller later said that no other plane had been in the sky that night, which surprised him.
3. Both stories show that fear can be overcome. The young seagull conquers his fear of flying with the push of hunger and his mother's tricks. The pilot, in danger, trusts the mysterious plane and lands safely. Both discover that courage and trust lead to success.
